title: Redwood POC Weekly Sync - Lunaris Analytics (cost/econ)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review updated throughput/cost benchmarks, discuss caching and batching tradeoffs from the last run, and align next steps for a 48h load test and security docs. Customer is focused on tokens/sec/$, prefix caching savings and whether Dedicated vs hosted makes sense for production cost targets.
topics: next steps for load test and security docs
next_steps: Redwood to share updated benchmark spreadsheet with cost-per-token and tokens/sec for the 2 models tested (Priya)
Lunaris to confirm target 95p latency SLO and peak qps for 48h run (Samir)
Redwood to enable prefix-cache run on staging and share results (Diego)
Redwood to circulate SOC2 summary and network diagram for Private offering (Alex)
Schedule executive sync after 48h run to review go/no-go (Tara/Jordan)
action_items: Priya Nair: upload annotated benchmark sheet by 2026-03-06
Samir Patel: confirm peak qps target and provide sample requests by 2026-03-05
Diego Morales: run prefix-caching experiment on staging and report token savings by 2026-03-09
Alex Kim: send SOC2 summary + Private deployment network diagram by 2026-03-08
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Morning everyone, thanks for joining, we' ll kick off — agenda is cost econ results, caching, batching tradeoffs and next steps.
[00:10] Samir (Lunaris): Hey, yeah, thanks. we ran the last benchmark overnight, so we have some numbers — a little noisy but interesting.
[00:20] Priya (Redwood SE): quick note — the run used the 8-bit quantized variant on A100s, continuous batching with max batch 32, and prefix KV cache enabled for 30% of traffic.
[00:35] Jordan (Lunaris SRE): real quick, our goal for pilot is to hit about 400 reqs/s peak and 95th < 300ms for short completions, is that still feasible?
[00:45] Priya: for the current model variant, tokens/sec we observed ~18k tokens/sec per GPU in steady state, cost per million tokens came to about $28 on the Dedicated estimate; hosted estimate slightly higher due to margin.
[00:58] Tara (CTO): that cost seems a bit above our internal target — we were hoping for sub-$20 per M tokens in production. where are the savings coming from?
[01:08] Alex: good call; biggest lever is KV/prefix caching and batching. in the last run caching reduced tokens processed by ~22% across the traffic mix because Lunaris has a lot of repeated prefixes in analytics prompt scaffolding.
[01:20] Samir: hmm 22% is promising. how reliable is that across user traffic? our sample set may over-represent repeated queries.
[01:30] Priya: noted — our staging trace was 40% of requests having medium-length shared prefixes (dashboard prompts). if production skews differently savings could be lower; we recommend running a 48h capture and compute prefix-uniqueness.
[01:45] Jordan: can caching cause correctness issues? our QA worried about stale KV state between users.
[01:55] Priya: caching is prefix-based and namespaced per customer/session; Redwood's runtime isolates KV caches per route, but we still advise TTLs and conservative invalidation for now.
[02:05] Samir: ok. what about batching — we saw batching improve tokens/sec but latency spiked for some short requests. details?
[02:15] Priya: yes, batching increases throughput but adds queuing latency. with max batch 32 and target latency SLO 300ms, p95 for short prompts was 420ms. lowering max batch to 8 dropped p95 to 210ms but reduced tokens/sec by ~28%.
[02:30] Tara: tradeoff then is cost vs latency — we prefer sub-300ms but also need cost predictability. any middle ground?
[02:40] Priya: adaptive batching is an option — dynamic batch windows based on queue depth to favor latency-sensitive traffic. we can prioritize low-latency routes and use larger batches for background scoring.
[02:55] Alex: customers often split routes: interactive endpoints (low batch) and async scoring (high batch), that gives best unit-econ while keeping UX snappy.
[03:05] Samir: can Redwood route by route and apply different batching/caching policies?
[03:10] Diego (Redwood): yes — per-route config with traffic tags. we can also set fallback policies if Dedicated capacity saturated.
[03:18] Jordan: about Dedicated vs hosted — Dedicated price was lower in your estimate, but committed capacity is a contract. any hybrid options?
[03:26] Alex: hybrid routing we mentioned earlier: warm Dedicated pool plus hosted overflow; reduces commit size and keeps costs contained. many customers do that during spikey periods.
[03:36] Tara: our security team will need network diagrams, KMS details, audit log retention for Private. alex — you said you'd share docs?
[03:43] Alex: yes, i will send SOC2 summary and network diagram by monday, including KMS options and audit retention settings.
[03:50] Samir: back to numbers — can you walk me through tokens/sec/$ calc?
[03:55] Priya: sure, we computed tokens/sec/$ as (measured tokens/sec per GPU) / (per-GPU cost per second). per-GPU cost derived from host price + infra overhead. for the quantized variant we used $2.5/hr per GPU in Dedicated amortized — that's the estimate in spreadsheet.
[04:15] Samir: is that including storage and net egress? we have heavy downstream storage for embeddings and logs.
[04:22] Alex: egress/storage not fully in that per-token; we'll add a line for ancillary costs in updated sheet. good catch.
[04:28] Priya: also note quantization impact: 8-bit gives similar quality for most prompts but reduces memory and increases tokens/sec, 4-bit is riskier for some of your prompts with long-context math. we left quantization recommendations in the notes column.
[04:44] Tara: we need the quality-impact assessment documented — if it reduces response fidelity we can't trade that for cost.
[04:50] Priya: agreed; we did a small eval set (100 prompts) and saw minor regressions on technical instructions; we can expand eval to match Lunaris' critical prompts.
[04:58] Samir: for the 48h run — what config will you use? we want to mirror production as close as possible.
[05:04] Diego: propose two runs: run A — per-route config with adaptive batching (low-latency route max batch 8, background 32), prefix-caching enabled; run B — same but with prefix-caching disabled to quantify savings. both on Dedicated pool sized to your peak qps estimate.
[05:20] Jordan: timeline?
[05:22] Alex: we can start the capture immediately; once Samir provides sample traffic we'll schedule the 48h starting 3/8 and finish 3/10, report 3/11.
[05:30] Priya: action items recap — we'll upload annotated benchmark sheet, Diego will run cache experiment on staging, and Alex sends SOC2 and network diagram.
[05:38] Tara: sounds good. also, can you include cost modeling for hybrid route (Dedicated + hosted overflow) and show sensitivity to 10%/20% traffic spikes?
[05:46] Alex: yes, we will add a scenario tab in the benchmark sheet.
[05:50] Samir: ok thanks all, that helps.
[05:53] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and schedule.
